subject.title: [Feature] Re-enable dev channel distribution tag for npm releases

question: Should packaged development updates use npm `alpha` while `dev` becomes git-only, or should OpenClaw operate a separate moving-main npm `dev` channel?
rationale: Current source supports two different development concepts but does not define their permanent relationship; the choice affects public update semantics and security-sensitive release operations, so repository evidence cannot safely decide it without release-owner intent.

options.title: Use alpha for packages
options.body: Expose alpha as the packaged edge channel, keep dev for git `main`, and migrate the current package-dev documentation and behavior explicitly.

options.title: Publish separate dev snapshots
options.body: Add a distinct moving-main npm dev pipeline with defined versioning, retention, trigger, credential, provenance, and post-publish verification rules.

options.title: Remove packaged edge updates
options.body: Keep dev git-only and alpha release-internal, with package users limited to stable, extended-stable, and beta.

recommendation.title: Use alpha for packages
recommendation.body: Expose alpha as the packaged edge channel, keep dev for git `main`, and migrate the current package-dev documentation and behavior explicitly.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the dev channel and has the strongest recent history on release workflow policy and safeguards.
